title: YATRI Mock Hub - Time and Work

questions.solution: LCM of 15,20 = 60. Efficiency: A=4, B=3 units/day. Work done together in 4 days = (4+3)x4 = 28 units. Remaining = 60-28 = 32/60 = 8/15.

LCM of 30,45,90 = 90. Efficiency: A=3, B=2, C=1. In every 5-day cycle: A alone for 4 days + all three on the 5th day = 3x4 + 6x1 = 18 units. Since 18 units take 5 days, 90 units (full work) take 90x5/18 = 25 days.
Time is inversely proportional to efficiency. Efficiency ratio P:Q = 5:2, so time ratio P:Q = 2:5. Since P takes 12 days (=2 units), 1 unit = 6 days, so Q's time (5 units) = 30 days.
LCM of 12,15,20 = 60. Efficiency: (A+B)=5, (B+C)=4, (C+A)=3. Sum = 12 = 2x(A+B+C), so (A+B+C)=6. Efficiency of A = 6-4 = 2. Time for A alone = 60/2 = 30 days.
LCM of 16,12,4 = 48. Efficiency: A=3, B=4. (A+B+C) efficiency = 48/4 = 12. Efficiency of C = 12-3-4 = 5. Time for C alone = 48/5 = 9(3/5) days.

LCM of 8,3 = 24. Efficiency: A(building)=3, B(breaking)=-8. A alone for 4 days = 12 units. Then A+B for 2 days = (3-8)x2 = -10 units. Net so far = 12-10 = 2 units. Remaining = 24-2 = 22 units. Time for A alone = 22/3 = 7(1/3) days.
In 8 seconds, water filled = 0.375 x 8 = 3.0 litres.
LCM of 8,12 = 24. Efficiency: A=3, B=2. Work done together in 3 days = (3+2)x3 = 15 units. Remaining = 24-15 = 9 units = 9/24 = 3/8.

LCM of 12,16 = 48. A and B work together for the first 5 days, then B and C work together for the next 2 days (making B's total 7 days), then C works alone for the remaining 11 days (making C's total 2+11=13 days). Using efficiencies: (A+B)x5 + (B+C)x2 + C x n = 48, solving gives efficiency of C = 2 units, so time for C alone = 48/2 = 24 days.
Using efficiencies scaled so all three finish together in 5 days: efficiency ratio A:B:C = 15:10:11 (sum 36). Since payment is proportional to work contributed, C's share = 7200x11/36 = Rs.2,200.

Time ratio A:B = 3:2. Since B takes 18 hours (2 units), 1 unit = 9 hours, so A takes 27 hours. Efficiency ratio A:B = 2:3 (inverse of time). Total work = 27x2 = 54 units. Combined efficiency = 2+3=5. Time together = 54/5 = 10.8 hours.

Efficiency ratio A:B = 3:1, so time ratio A:B = 1:3. Let time A = x, time B = 3x. Difference = 2x = 60, so x=30. Time A=30, Time B=90. Total work = 90x1 = 90 (or 30x3). Combined efficiency = 3+1=4. Time together = 90/4 = 22.5 days.
LCM of 12,18 = 36. Efficiency: A=3, B=2. Work done together in 4 days = (3+2)x4 = 20 units. Remaining = 36-20 = 16 units. Time for A alone = 16/3 = 5(1/3) days.
(A+B)x30 = Ax16 + Bx44. So 30A+30B=16A+44B, giving 14A=14B, i.e. A=B (equal efficiency). Total work = (A+B)x30 = 2Ax30 = 60A. Time for B alone = 60A/A = 60 days.
LCM of 20,30,60 = 60. Efficiency: A=3, B=2, C=1. Per 3-day cycle: Day1(A alone)=3, Day2(A alone)=3, Day3(A+B+C)=6. Total per 3 days = 12 units. In 15 days (5 cycles) = 60 units = full work.

LCM of 28,35 = 140. Efficiency: A=5, B=4. Work done by B alone in 17 days = 17x4=68. Remaining (worked together before A left) = 140-68=72. Combined rate = 5+4=9. Days worked together = 72/9 = 8 days.

Efficiency ratio A:B = 1:2. First 25% work done by A alone. Remaining 75% done by both (combined rate=3 units). A's contribution in this phase = (1/3)x75%=25%. So A's total contribution = 25%+25%=50%, B's = 50%. B's share = 50% of 840 = Rs.420.
Combined rate = 4/3 + 3/4 = 16/12+9/12 = 25/12 litres per minute. Time for 100 litres = 100/(25/12) = 100x12/25 = 48 minutes.
Total work is equal: 20Wx16 = 10Mx12. So M/W = (20x16)/(10x12) = 320/120 = 8/3. Ratio M:W = 8:3.
Efficiency ratio A:B = 5:4 (since 25% more = 5/4). Percentage of work done by A = 5/(5+4) x 100% = 500/9% = 55.56%.
LCM of 4,8 = 8. Efficiency: Sujit=2, Rakesh=1. Work done together in 2 days = (2+1)x2 = 6 units. Remaining work = 8-6=2 units. Percentage left = 2/8 x 100% = 25%.
Area of trapezium base = (1/2)x(sum of parallel sides)xheight = (1/2)x(10+6)x4 = (1/2)x16x4 = 32 cm^2. Volume of prism = base area x prism height = 32x15 = 480 cm^3.

Since 5 men alone and 12 women alone both take 70 days for the same total work, 5M=12W in total capacity, giving M:W=12:5. Using M=12,W=5: Total work=5x12x70=4200. Combined (5M+12W) rate = 5x12+12x5=120. Time = 4200/120 = 35 days.
Rate = 120/6 = 20 bottles per minute. In 14 minutes = 20x14 = 280 bottles.
LCM of 12,20 = 60. Efficiency: (Dhaval+Dhiraj)=5, Dhaval=3. Efficiency of Dhiraj = 5-3=2. Time for Dhiraj alone = 60/2=30 days.

Let total work=50 units (LCM based). Efficiency of Chetan=1. Athar's efficiency equals Baban+Chetan's combined efficiency (given). Also (Athar+Baban) efficiency=5 (since total/10=5). So (Baban+Chetan+Baban)=5, i.e. 2xBaban+1=5, giving Baban=2. Time for Baban alone = 50/2=25 days.
Using M1D1=M2D2: 15x20=20xD2. So D2 = 300/20 = 15 days.

Since 10 men and 15 women alone both take 170 days for the same work, 10M=15W in capacity, giving M:W=3:2. Using M=3,W=2: Total work=10x3x170=5100. Combined(20M+20W) rate=20x3+20x2=100. Time=5100/100=51 days.

From the two statements, we only get the combined efficiency ratio (Q+R):(P+R) = 3:2. This does not let us separate out the individual efficiencies of P, Q and R, so we cannot determine how long all three working together would take, even using both statements combined.
LCM of 15,20=60. Efficiency: A=4, B=3. Combined time = 60/7 = 8.57 days (approx 8.5 days).
Total work = efficiency of A x time of A = 2x40=80 units. In 5 days, all three together do (2+3+5)x5=50 units. Remaining=80-50=30 units. A+B rate=2+3=5. Time=30/5=6 days.
LCM of 6,12,18 = 36. Efficiency: (A+B+C)=6, A=3, B=2. Efficiency of C = 6-3-2=1. Time for C alone = 36/1 = 36 days.

LCM of 15,25=75. Efficiency: Lalit=5, Laxman=3. Lalit+Laxman(5 days)=(5+3)x5=40. Remaining=75-40=35 units, done by Lalit+Deven in 4 days, combined rate=8.75. Efficiency of Deven=8.75-5=3.75. Time for Deven alone=75/3.75=20 days.
LCM of 30,40=120. Efficiency: A=4, B=3. A+B(10 days)=(4+3)x10=70. Remaining=120-70=50 units, done by A+B+C in 5 days, combined rate=10. Efficiency of C=10-7=3. Time for C alone=120/3=40 days.
Total work = 10x16=160 worker-days. Work done in 4 days by 10 workers=40. Remaining=120. Now 8 workers remain. Time = 120/8=15 days.

LCM of 20,30=60. Efficiency: P=3, Q=2. P+Q(6 days)=(3+2)x6=30. Remaining=60-30=30, done by P+R in 8 days, combined rate=3.75. Efficiency of R=3.75-3=0.75. Time for R to complete 60% of work = (0.6x60)/0.75 = 48 days.
Total work = 15x8x24=2880 man-hours. Work done in first 6 days=15x8x6=720. Remaining=2160 man-hours. Now 20 men work 6 hours/day = 120 man-hours/day. Days needed = 2160/120 = 18 days.
Since both groups take equal time (10 days) for the same work, (6W+4M) = (4W+5M) in capacity, giving 2W=M. Total work = (6W+4x2W)x10 = 140W. Time for 8 women = 140W/8W = 17.5 days.
Hourly wage = 52.50/3.5 = 15. As a fraction, this is 15/1.
Hourly wage = 52.50/3.5 = 15. As a fraction, this is 15/1.
Total work = 20x45=900 man-days. Work done by 60 men in 6 days = 60x6=360 man-days. Percentage = 360/900x100 = 40%.
Total work = 66Wx79. Time for 6 women to complete 1/11th of total work = (66x79)/(11x6) = 5214/66 = 79 days.
LCM of 10,15=30. Efficiency: A=3, B=2. A's 4 days alone = 12 units. Remaining = 30-12=18 units. Combined rate=5. Additional days = 18/5 = 3.6 days.
LCM of 10,15=30. Efficiency: (A+B)=3, B=2. Efficiency of A = 3-2=1. Time for A alone = 30/1=30 days.
LCM of 12,36=36. Efficiency: A=3, B=1. Combined=4. Time = 36/4=9 days.
LCM of 15,30=30. Efficiency: A=2, B=1. A+B(5 days)=(2+1)x5=15. Remaining=30-15=15. Time for B alone = 15/1=15 days.
LCM of 8,12,16=48. Efficiency: (A+B+C)=6, (A+B)=4. Efficiency of C=(A+B+C)-(A+B)=6-4=2. Time for C alone = 48/2=24 days.
Work done in 6 days = 6/30 = 1/5.
LCM of 12,24=24. Efficiency: A=2, B=1. A+B(4 days)=(2+1)x4=12. Remaining=24-12=12. Time for B alone = 12/1=12 days.
LCM of 18,27=54. Efficiency: A=3, B=2. A+B(6 days)=(3+2)x6=30. Remaining=54-30=24. Time for B alone = 24/2=12 days.
Efficiency ratio Man:Boy = 2:1, total 3 units. Daily total pay = 600/5=120. Boy's daily share = 120x(1/3)=Rs.40.

LCM of 15,25=75. Efficiency: Amit=5, Baban=3. Amit+Baban(5 days)=(5+3)x5=40. Remaining=75-40=35, done by Amit+Chetan in 4 days, combined rate=8.75. Efficiency of Chetan=8.75-5=3.75. Time for Chetan alone=75/3.75=20 days.

Let total work=40 units. Efficiency of C=1. Given A's efficiency equals (B+C)'s combined efficiency. Also (A+B) efficiency=4 (since 40/10=4). So (B+C+B)=4, i.e. 2B+1=4, giving B=1.5, so A=B+C=1.5+1=2.5. Time for A alone=40/2.5=16 days.
LCM of 16,12=48. Efficiency: A=3, B=4. B's work in 8 days=32. Remaining=48-32=16. Time for A alone=16/3=5(1/3) days = 5 days 8 hours.
LCM of 12,15,20=60. Efficiency: A=5, B=4, C=3. Per 3-day cycle = 5+4+3=12 units. In 15 days (5 cycles) = 60 units = full work.
(4B+6G)x8 = (3B+7G)x10. So 32B+48G=30B+70G, giving 2B=22G, B=11G. Total work = (4x11G+6G)x8 = 50Gx8=400G. Time for 10 girls = 400G/10G = 40 days.
Using M1D1=M2D2: 8x14=12xD2. So D2 = 112/12 = 9.33 days.

A's rate for 60% work in 18 days means A alone would take 18/0.6=30 days for the full work. Total work=30 units (A's efficiency=1). Remaining 40%=12 units, done by A+B together in 4 days, combined rate=3. Efficiency of B=3-1=2. Time for B alone = 30/2=15 days.
LCM of 8,16=16. Efficiency: (A+B)=2, A=1. Efficiency of B=1. Time for B alone = 16/1=16 days.
Efficiency ratio Sonu:Monu = 4:5 (since Sonu is 20% less efficient). Total work = 30x(4+5) = 270 units. Sonu completes 40% = 0.4x270=108 units. Time = 108/4=27 days.
Total work = 18x20=360 man-days. Work done in 10 days=18x10=180. Remaining=180. Remaining men=12. Time = 180/12=15 days.
LCM of 6,12=12. Efficiency: (A+B)=2, A=1. Efficiency of B=1. Time for B alone=12/1=12 days.
LCM of 8,16=16. Efficiency: A=2, B=1. Combined=3. Time = 16/3 = 5(1/3) days.
LCM of 15,25=75. Efficiency: (A+B)=5, A=3. Efficiency of B=2. Time for B alone=75/2=37.5 days.
(6M+8B)x10 = (26M+48B)x2. So 60M+80B=52M+96B, giving 8M=16B, M=2B. Total work = (6x2B+8B)x10=200B. Combined (15M+20B) = 15x2B+20B=50B. Time = 200B/50B = 4 days.
LCM of 15,20=60. Efficiency: A=4, B=3. Work done together in 5 days=(4+3)x5=35. Remaining=60-35=25/60=5/12.
LCM of 12,20=60. Efficiency: (A+B)=5, A=3. Efficiency of B=5-3=2. Time for B alone=60/2=30 days.
LCM of 9,18=18. Efficiency: (A+B)=2, A=1. Efficiency of B=1. Time for B alone=18/1=18 days.
LCM of 25,30=150. Efficiency: Mohit=6, Rohit=5. Ratio 6:5, total 11 units = 6600, so 1 unit = 600. Mohit's share=6x600=3600, Rohit's=5x600=3000. Difference=600.

LCM of 5,15=15. Efficiency: P=3, Q=1. Day1(P)=3, Day2(Q)=1, per 2-day cycle=4 units. In 6 days (3 cycles)=12 units. Remaining=15-12=3 units. Day7 (P's turn) completes exactly 3 units, finishing the work. Total=7 days.
(P+Q)x24 = (P+Q)x8 + Qx20. So (P+Q)x16=Qx20, giving 16P+16Q=20Q, so 16P=4Q, Q=4P. Ratio P:Q=1:4. Total work=(1+4)x24=120. Time for P alone=120/1=120 days.
LCM of 12,24=24. Efficiency: P=2, Q=1. Day1(P)=2, Day2(Q)=1, per 2-day cycle=3 units. In 16 days (8 cycles)=24 units=full work exactly.
LCM of 6,9=18. Efficiency: (A+B)=3, A=2. Efficiency of B=1. Time for B alone=18/1=18 days.

Let A's total work=24 units (rate=1/day). After A's first 6 days, work done=6 units, remaining=18 units. This remaining work is completed by (A+sister) together in 10 days, so their combined rate=18/10=1.8. Sister's rate=1.8-1=0.8. Time for sister alone=24/0.8=30 days.
LCM of 8,12,16=48. Efficiency: (A+B)=6, (B+C)=4, (C+A)=3. Sum of all pairs=13=2x(A+B+C), so (A+B+C)=6.5. Efficiency of A=6.5-4=2.5. Time for A alone=48/2.5=19.2 days.
Efficiency ratio Prakash:Jayesh = 1:2. Total work=1x15=15 units. Combined efficiency=1+2=3. Time = 15/3=5 days.
(A+B)x20 = Ax15 + Bx42. So 20A+20B=15A+42B, giving 5A=22B, A/B=22/5. Total work=(22+5)x20=540 (using A=22,B=5 as scaled efficiency units). Time for B alone=540/5=108 days.
Efficiency ratio A:B = 5:4 (since A is 25% more efficient). Percentage of work by A = 5/9 x 100% = 55.56%.
LCM of 10,20,30=60. Efficiency: (A+B+C)=6, A=3, B=2. Efficiency of C=6-3-2=1. Time for C alone=60/1=60 days.
LCM of 2,4=4. Efficiency: X=2, Y=1. Combined=3. Time=4/3 days = 1(1/3) days.
Total work = 6x8=48 worker-days. With 10 workers, time = 48/10 = 4.8 days.
Since 5 men and 8 women both take 12 days for the same total work, 5M=8W, giving M:W=8:5. Using M=8,W=5: Total work=5x8x12=480. Combined (10M+4W) = 10x8+4x5=80+20=100. Time=480/100=4.8 days.

LCM of 24,30,40=120. Efficiency: P=5, Q=4, R=3. In the first 8 days (P+Q+R): (5+4+3)x8=96. Remaining=120-96=24. Let T be additional days needed; Q works (T-6) days and R works T days (since Q leaves 6 days before completion). (Q+R)(T-6) + Rx6 = 24: (4+3)(T-6)+3x6=24, so 7(T-6)=6, T-6=6/7, T=48/7. Total time=8+48/7=(56+48)/7=104/7 days.
Efficiency ratio A:B=2:1. Total work=12x(2+1)=36. Time for A alone=36/2=18 days.

LCM of 15,20,30=60. Efficiency: P=4, Q=3, R=2. In the first 4 days (P+Q+R): (4+3+2)x4=36. Remaining=60-36=24. Let T be additional days; Q works (T-6) days and R works T days. (Q+R)(T-6)+Rx6=24: (3+2)(T-6)+2x6=24, so 5(T-6)=12, T-6=12/5, T=42/5. Total time=4+42/5=(20+42)/5=62/5 days.
LCM of 20,30=60. Efficiency: A=3, B=2. A+B(6 days)=(3+2)x6=30. Remaining=60-30=30. Time for B alone=30/2=15 days.
LCM of 10,15=30. Efficiency: A=3, B=2. A's first 4 days=12. Remaining=30-12=18. Combined rate=5. Additional days=18/5=3.6. Total time=4+3.6=7.6 days.
Sudhir's rate = 40/8=5 pages/hour. Combined rate = 350/35=10 pages/hour. Prakash's rate = 10-5=5 pages/hour. Time for Prakash to type 40 pages = 40/5=8 hours.
Using M1D1=M2D2: 8x10=4xD2. So D2 = 80/4 = 20 days.
Let total work = LCM(10,25) = 50 units. Efficiency: (A+B)=5, B=2. Efficiency of A=5-2=3. Given A's efficiency equals (B+C)'s combined efficiency: 3=2+C, so C=1. Time for C alone=50/1=50 days.
Efficiency ratio A:B=2:1, so time ratio A:B=1:2. Let time A=x, time B=2x. Difference=2x-x=x=10 days. So time A=10 days, time B=20 days.
LCM of 6,8,3=24. Efficiency: A=4, B=3. (A+B+C) efficiency=24/3=8. Efficiency of C=8-4-3=1. C's share=(1/8)x3200=Rs.400.

Efficiency ratio A:B=4:1, so time ratio A:B=1:4. Let time A=x, time B=4x. Difference=4x-x=3x=45, so x=15. Time A=15, time B=60. Total work=15x4=60 units. Combined efficiency=4+1=5. Time together=60/5=12 days.
5M+2B = 3(M+B). So 5M+2B=3M+3B, giving 2M=B, meaning M:B=1:2.
Total items = 30x45=1350. New number of rows = 1350/25 = 54.
LCM of 18,30=90. Efficiency: (A+B)=5, A=3. Efficiency of B=2. Time for B alone=90/2=45 days.
Efficiency ratio A:B=2:1. Total work=12x(2+1)=36. Time for B alone=36/1=36 days.

LCM of 15,20=60. Efficiency: A=4, B=3. Days 1,2 (A+B together)=(4+3)x2=14; Day 3 (A alone, since B is absent)=4. Total per 3-day cycle=18 units. In 9 days (3 cycles)=54 units. Remaining=60-54=6. Day 10 is an (A+B) day at combined rate 7; time needed = 6/7 of a day. Total=9+6/7 = 9(6/7) days.

LCM of 12,15,20=60. Efficiency: A=5, B=4, C=3. In 4 days (A+B+C): (5+4+3)x4=48. Remaining=60-48=12. B+C's normal combined rate=4+3=7; at 3/4 rate = 21/4=5.25. Additional days=12/5.25 = 48/21 = 16/7 = 2(2/7) days.
A's total work units = 7x2=14. B's total work units = 5x4=20. Ratio A:B=14:20=7:10. Since A's share (7 parts) = 4900, 1 part = 700. B's share (10 parts) = 10x700 = Rs.7,000.
